claim_summary: TimeXL contributes a prototype-based multimodal encoder plus prediction, reflection, and refinement LLMs that iteratively improve multimodal time-series predictions and explanations.

claim_evidence.quote: we introduce TimeXL, a multi-modal prediction framework that integrates a prototypebased time series encoder with three collaborating Large Language Models (LLMs) to deliver more accurate predictions and interpretable explanations.

modules.name: Multimodal prototype-based encoder
modules.scope_reason: R2: the encoder is a separate convolutional prototype classifier; the LLM never receives its embeddings, only selected prototype text, so it does not change how the model represents temporal inputs and is a Harness tool, not LLM side. R3_1_TSK: its objective is cross-entropy on discrete labels with class-wise prototypes; a different task family needs a different output head and loss.
rubric_path: R2:Harness - model invoked beside the LLM, LLM sees only text
R3_1_TSK:yes - discrete-label prediction objective and class prototypes

evidence.quote: We design a multi-modal prototype-based encoder that can generate predictions and explanations across different modalities in an end-to-end manner, as shown in Figure 2.

modules.name: Prototype-conditioned prediction fusion
modules.scope_reason: Top-omega prototype-segment pairs are retrieved and added to the prediction LLM prompt, then encoder and LLM probabilities are linearly fused with alpha tuned on validation data; R3_1_TSK: fusion target is the task's prediction probability, and the retrieved cases are class prototypes.
rubric_path: R2:Harness - prompt and fusion, no parameter update of the LLM
R3_1_TSK:yes - prediction output and validation-tuned fusion
R4:Memory and Context; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: We compile the final prediction based on a fusion of both the multi-modal encoder Menc and prediction LLM Mpred.
To improve prediction accuracy, the encoder Menc supplements s with case-based explanations.

modules.name: Reflection-driven context refinement
modules.scope_reason: The reflection compares prediction with ground truth and the refinement changes text and retrains the encoder for later prediction iterations; changing the prediction task changes the validation target and refinement objective, so R3_1_TSK applies.
rubric_path: R4:Planning and Orchestration; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: the reflection agent Mrefl aims to understand the reasoning behind the implicit prediction logic of Mpred. Specifically, it generates a reflective feedback, Refl, by analyzing the input text s and its prediction ŷ LLM , against the ground truth y, to provide actionable insights for refinement
Once the textual context is improved, it is used to retrain the multimodal prototype-based encoder Menc for the next iteration.

task_performance.quote: TimeXL constantly achieves the highest F1 and AUC scores, consistently surpassing both time series and multi-modal baselines by up to 8.9% of AUC (compared to TimeCAP on the Weather dataset).

items.reason: Prediction LLM is queried as Mpred(s, expls) with prototype text only; the encoder never feeds embeddings to the LLM and no LLM is trained, so R2 LLM side and representation_alignment do not apply.

adjudication.summary: The candidate's LLM-side encoder was rejected: the encoder is a standalone prototype classifier whose outputs reach the LLM only as text. Modules are TSK with fusion and refinement labels adjusted.
